verdict: Avoid new unsecured spice-trade exposure in Sangli; lend only to licensed, FDA-clean processors with stock-and-receivables control, and treat the rest as watchlist.
title: Sangli Spices Processing & Trade: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**A Sangli spice unit buys raw chilli, coriander and masala inputs in the February-to-June arrival window, cleans, grinds, blends and packs, and sells into retail and festive demand.** Cash is locked in stock first and receivables second; the ICRA peer note puts net working capital over operating income at around 45% as on March 31, 2025, improved from 51% in FY2024 [9]. Utilisation peaks July to November, typically till Diwali [10] — so when a proposal lands, check whether the drawing power is built for that peak, not the annual average. ## What has changed now
**Input costs are the swing factor: chilli and coriander inflation climbed 78% and 40% respectively, and the peer passed it through with pricing contributing 11.4% to growth [6].** That is a pricing-power test, not a demand test. Local demand is shifting toward ready-made festive faral in Sangli [1], which favours packers with brand and shelf presence over plain grinders. Avoid pure traders holding loose stock against price bets, and avoid any unit whose licence file is thin [2]. ## How to grow safely
**Structure against the stock, not the balance sheet: cash credit or stock-and-receivable limits with monthly stock statements, and a charge on current assets.** Take every month the stock statement with ageing, the GST return, and the sales register split by customer. Cap unsecured exposure; insist on promoter contribution for any new capex, since the peer's own FY2027 capex of Rs 15-20 crore and repayments of around Rs 54 crore are serviced from cash flows [10]. A sudden shift from branded packing to loose trade, or pricing that lags input inflation [6], signals margin erosion. Sangli-specific published data on this trade is thin; the local paper covers demand and enforcement, not unit economics, so lean on first principles and the peer and rating evidence above.

## The call
**The data-based call is AVOID at 44, and the local news flow — enforcement action and cost inflation — does not improve it.** Maharashtra electricity demand grew 6.0% Apr-to-date against India's 9.5% [D], a slower local signal, while state GST collections grew 8.6% against India's 6.1% [D]. India-wide exports fell 5.7% Apr-to-date in USD [D], and bank credit grew 26.3% YoY against output growth of 5.1% [D]. **Lend selectively to licensed, branded processors; avoid the trading end of this market.**
